Read accessions into entry, isoform or version, and applied variants, with mzLib

proteins_parse_accessions.Rd

Read protein accessions back into their entry, isoform or version, and applied sequence variants, with mzLib's accession grammars, never repairing one that does not fit.

Answers **which entry, isoform and variants does P04637-2_S70N or NP_000537.3_R72P name?** Wraps mzLib's VariantApplication.ParseAccession (mzLib #1382), and through it ProteinAccession.Parse. It is the inverse of the names mzLib gives variant proteoforms: P04637_S70N is entry P04637 with S70N applied, and NP_000537.3_R72P is RefSeq NP_000537, version 3, with R72P. Use it to link a search result's accession to anything you keep per entry - genes, orthologs, GO terms - without losing the isoform or the variants. Cutting at the first _ would turn NP_000537 into NP.

Usage

proteins_parse_accessions(accessions, timeout = NULL)

Arguments

accessions

A character vector, one accession per result row, in order, duplicates included. Sent on stdin, unchanged: not trimmed, not split. A blank or NA entry, or one with a line break, is refused, because it would shift every later row.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL (the default) to wait.

Details

It parses and never repairs. An accession outside UniProt's and RefSeq's protein grammars comes back "unrecognized" and verbatim - lower case, a stray space, a FASTA header, a DECOY_ prefix, a |-joined protein group, and P12345_2, mzLib's loader counter for a *different* entry whose accession collided. mzLibR sends each accession exactly as you give it.

Value

An mzlibr_parsed_accessions. record_count counts the accessions parsed, duplicates included. namespace_counts is a named vector, namespace to the number of accessions in it, every namespace present (uniprot, refseq, unrecognized), zeros included: a large unrecognized count is worth reading, see caveats. with_applied_variants_count counts the accessions that name applied variants. caveats says what mzLib leaves unrecognized rather than repairs.

records is a data.frame with one row per accession, in the order given: input, exactly as given; entry_accession, the UniProt entry or unversioned RefSeq accession (P04637 for P04637-2_S70N), equal to input when unrecognized - an entry, not a sequence; isoform, the UniProt -n number, NA without one (always for RefSeq) or past 2,147,483,647; version, the RefSeq .n number, NA without one (always for UniProt) or past 2,147,483,647; namespace; parent_accession, the entry the variants were applied to, isoform or version kept (P04637-2 for P04637-2_Q5*), equal to input without variants; applied_variants, the suffix as written (S70N_A80T), NA without one; and has_applied_variants.

Joining on it

entry_accession answers "same entry?", not "same sequence?": P04637 and P04637-2 share it, but they are different sequences. Join per-entry data on it, and sequence-level data on input. namespace is spelled as proteins_resolve_genes spells it, so the two tables join. setNames(parsed$records$entry_accession, parsed$records$input) maps each accession to its entry, for grouping.

Wraps

Wire verb proteins parse-accession. Generated from the bridge's verb spec proteins.parse-accession.yaml (bridge commit aea14604d5f7) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • ProteoformAccession in mzLib/Omics/BioPolymer/ProteoformAccession.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ProteinAccession.Parse in mzLib/MzLibUtil/ProteinAccession.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • AccessionNamespace in mzLib/MzLibUtil/ProteinAccession.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

accessions

string[]; required; range >= 1 line. Read from stdin (not an option): one accession per line, given to mzLib exactly as read, with no trimming, case folding or splitting. Blank lines are skipped. One row per line, in input order, duplicates included.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

record_count

int; in accessions; never NA. Rows: the input accessions.

namespace_counts

map<string,int>; in accessions; never NA. Namespace -> accessions in it; all three keys (unrecognized, uniprot, refseq) always present, zeros included.

with_applied_variants_count

int; in accessions; never NA. Accessions that name applied variants (has_applied_variants true).

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. Column name to one value per input, in input order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Seven static caveats.

Columns of records

input

string; never NA. The line exactly as read (ProteoformAccession.Verbatim).

entry_accession

string; never NA. The UniProt entry or unversioned RefSeq accession (ProteinAccession.EntryAccession): P04637 for P04637-2_S70N, NP_000537 for NP_000537.3_R72P. Equal to input when unrecognized. Names an entry, not a sequence.

isoform

int; NA when no UniProt -n isoform suffix (always null for RefSeq and unrecognized), or a number too large for a 32-bit integer. The UniProt isoform number (ProteinAccession.Isoform).

version

int; NA when no RefSeq .n version (always null for UniProt and unrecognized), or a number too large for a 32-bit integer. The RefSeq version (ProteinAccession.Version).

namespace

string; never NA. uniprot, refseq or unrecognized: mzLib's AccessionNamespace, lower case as genes resolve and mzLib's GeneResolutionTsv write it.

parent_accession

string; never NA. The accession of the entry the variants were applied to, as written, isoform or version kept (ProteoformAccession.Entry.Verbatim): P04637-2 for P04637-2_Q5*. Equal to input when there are no applied variants.

applied_variants

string; NA when the accession names no applied variant. The variant suffix as written, without the leading '_' (ProteoformAccession.AppliedVariants): S70N, or S70N_A80T for several.

has_applied_variants

bool; never NA. ProteoformAccession.HasAppliedVariants: applied_variants is not null.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

no accessions on stdin

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected: ParseAccession does not throw

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Parses, never repairs (mzLib's rule): an accession outside the UniProt and RefSeq protein grammars is unrecognized and kept verbatim, entry_accession equal to input. That includes lower case, surrounding spaces, a FASTA header (sp|P04637|P53_HUMAN), a decoy, contaminant or entrapment prefix (DECOY_P04637), and ProteinDbLoader's collision counter (P04637_2, which names a different entry whose accession collided).

  • entry_accession names the entry, not a sequence: P04637 and P04637-2 share it but are different sequences, and the isoform UniProt displays for an entry can carry any number. It answers 'same entry', never 'same sequence'.

  • A protein-group accession joined with '|' (P04637|P02768) is unrecognized as a whole: mzLib does not split it. Split protein groups first.

  • Only RefSeq protein accessions (NP_, XP_, YP_, WP_, AP_) are recognized; a RefSeq transcript (NM_) or an Ensembl id (ENSP...) is unrecognized.

  • A variant suffix is read only after an entry mzLib recognizes, in the form mzLib's GetAccession writes: '_', the original residues, a 1-based position, the variant residues (S70N; a deletion A80; a stop gain Q5*), repeated for several (S70N_A80T). applied_variants is that suffix as written: it is not checked against any sequence.

  • An isoform or version number too large for a 32-bit integer (over 2147483647) reads as null while the accession still counts as UniProt or RefSeq: mzLib keeps the entry and drops the number.

  • Each stdin line is one accession, given to mzLib exactly as read; blank lines are skipped. One row per line, in input order, duplicates included.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.proteins.parse_accessions

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::proteins::parse_accessions

  • R (mzLibR): proteins_parse_accessions

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • Whether to split '|'-joined protein-group accessions before parsing: mzLib does not, so the verb does not either. Splitting is a grouping rule, and it belongs in mzLib if anywhere.

  • An isoform or version past int.MaxValue is dropped with no signal while the namespace still reads uniprot or refseq (ProteinAccession.NumberOrNull). Whether mzLib should leave such an accession unrecognized instead is an mzLib question, not raised upstream yet.

  • Not yet ported to mzLibRust or mzLibR; the binding names above are proposals.

References

  • doi:10.1093/nar/gkae1010: UniProt, whose published accession grammar (and -n isoform suffix) mzLib matches (UniProt Consortium 2025, NAR)

  • doi:10.1093/nar/gkv1189: RefSeq, whose protein accession prefixes and .n versions mzLib matches (O'Leary et al. 2016, NAR)

See also

proteins_resolve_genes, proteins_read

Examples


parsed <- proteins_parse_accessions(c("P04637", "P04637-2", "Q13409-2", "NP_000537.3_R72P",
  "P04637_S70N_A80T", "P04637_2", "DECOY_P02768", "sp|P04637|P53_HUMAN", "P04637|P02768"))
parsed
#> <mzlibr_parsed_accessions> 9 accession(s), 2 with applied variants
#>   unrecognized 4, uniprot 4, refseq 1
#>   ! unrecognized ones are kept verbatim, never repaired: see $caveats
parsed$records[, c("input", "namespace", "entry_accession", "isoform", "version",
                   "applied_variants")]
#>                 input    namespace     entry_accession isoform version
#> 1              P04637      uniprot              P04637      NA      NA
#> 2            P04637-2      uniprot              P04637       2      NA
#> 3            Q13409-2      uniprot              Q13409       2      NA
#> 4    NP_000537.3_R72P       refseq           NP_000537      NA       3
#> 5    P04637_S70N_A80T      uniprot              P04637      NA      NA
#> 6            P04637_2 unrecognized            P04637_2      NA      NA
#> 7        DECOY_P02768 unrecognized        DECOY_P02768      NA      NA
#> 8 sp|P04637|P53_HUMAN unrecognized sp|P04637|P53_HUMAN      NA      NA
#> 9       P04637|P02768 unrecognized       P04637|P02768      NA      NA
#>   applied_variants
#> 1             <NA>
#> 2             <NA>
#> 3             <NA>
#> 4             R72P
#> 5        S70N_A80T
#> 6             <NA>
#> 7             <NA>
#> 8             <NA>
#> 9             <NA>
parsed$namespace_counts
#> unrecognized      uniprot       refseq 
#>            4            4            1
